slides.heading: Detect Arbitrage
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Detect Arbitrage, a very hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Exchange-rate matrix; is there a cycle of trades yielding profit?
Take -log(rate) edge weights and look for a negative cycle with Bellman-Ford.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Exchange-rate matrix; is there a cycle of trades yielding profit? Take -log(rate) edge weights and look for a negative cycle with Bellman-Ford.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Multiplying rates becomes adding minus logs, so profit means a negative cycle, found by Bellman-Ford.
slides.narration: Multiplying rates becomes adding minus logs, so profit means a negative cycle, found by Bellman-Ford.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Weights are minus log of the rate
2. Relax all edges n minus one times
3. If any edge still relaxes, there's arbitrage
slides.narration: Step by step. First, weights are minus log of the rate. Second, relax all edges n minus one times. Third, if any edge still relaxes, there's arbitrage.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n cubed. Space is O of n squared.
